items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: This Neil Fitzpatrick in Detroit didn't know whether I was white or black, he just didn't like the idea of "Loch Lomond" getting swung.

and there were times when I didn't feel like doing it but someone says, you know, you have to do this. This is part of the game, you know. All of a sudden I found myself very, very busy. Even when the selection of "Loch Lomond" was cut off the air. I mean, up until that time I don't suppose it made any difference who it was. It was just a swing version that mattered. This Neil Fitzpatrick in Detroit didn't know whether I was white or black, he just didn't like the idea of "Loch Lomond" getting swung.

Yes. Oh incidentally, we used the term I noticed in looking back over the early tapes, jazzing the classics okay, and that's kind of a very general term we used because it seems to me there are at least three things going on beyond that time, only one of which you were doing if I'm not mistaken. One would be making swing or jazz renditions of light classical music which I guess "Song of India" which Tommy Dorsey did, which was the first example, and many of the things that the Kirby Band did from "Chopin" and so…
